name: Odile Wark
bio: The fourth keeper of the Name-Kiln, a Greyfold potter's great-granddaughter, who has never let the kiln go out and never been further than Pilgrim's Ash. She presses each name into the clay with her thumbnail and a bone stylus, fires twelve at a time, and hangs them herself. She knows the screen by heart, row by row, and will tell you whose tile is clinking.
unique_habit: Says each name aloud as she presses it, and again as she hangs it, and if she has spelt it wrong she breaks the tile and starts again, however long it took.

appearance.notes: a leather apron grey to the knees with dried slip, sleeves rolled, forearms burnt in old pale patches, a bone stylus behind her ear

schedule.notes: drawing the kiln and hanging the day's tiles

name: Pell Hoddy
bio: A lay brother of the Tolling Order who has worked the lever of the Smoke-Speakers' Hood for twenty years, sleeping under the gantry. He can read the whole heath's smoke from the top of it, every chapter-house's straw-fire and every scavenger's cookfire, and he knows where everybody is and what they are saying, and has nobody to tell.
unique_habit: Counts under his breath in longs and shorts, even when he is talking, and taps them on whatever is to hand.

appearance.notes: the Order's grey gone brown at the shoulders with smoke, leather gloves to the elbow, eyes always narrowed, a knotted cord at his belt with the code on it

name: Wenna Thrope
bio: The Order's dial-reader on the west heath, a novice who was sent to learn the dial from the old reader and buried him a year later and stayed. She reads the shadow, rings the count on a hand-bell for the heath to hear, and keeps a tally of every hour in chalk on a board. She has worked out the Builders' numbers on the stones for herself and is very pleased about it.
unique_habit: Glances at the shadow whenever anybody says anything, as if the time might have changed what it means.

appearance.notes: a novice's grey with the sleeves cut off at the elbow, a brass hand-bell on a strap across her chest, chalk on both hands

schedule.notes: reading the shadow, ringing the hours

name: Aud Venn
bio: A sister of the Tolling Order and its hearer: the one sent when something on the heath makes a sound it should not. She came to the Fallen Head the day after Pell Hoddy's smoke, and has sat by its mouth since with a slate, writing down what it sings. She is not frightened of it. She is frightened of what the Order will do when it reads the slate.
unique_habit: Writes with her eyes shut, one hand flat on the slate to feel where the lines go.

appearance.notes: the Order's grey with a hearer's white cord round the neck, a slate on a strap, chalk-dust to the elbow, a small bronze bell with its clapper tied

schedule.notes: listening at the mouth: it sings at night

name: Ama Reedwright
bio: A stilt-walker of Isseva who heard from a Sayer that the Cistern of Isse had water in it again, and walked two regions to see it, on her stilts as far as the ash and on her feet after. The reedfolk say Isse walked up this stair out of the marsh; Ama has come to see if anything is walking up it now. She has not gone down. She says it is not hers to go down.
unique_habit: Stands on one leg when she is thinking, like a heron, and does not seem to notice she is doing it.

appearance.notes: Sedgish dyed blue at the hems gone grey with ash, her stilts tied on her back like a quiver, bare feet, a gourd on a cord

name: Corra Dunn
bio: A dyer from Merrowby who came south after her husband walked into the Hush in the spring, to walk after him. She got as far as the Leaving-Lines, hung up her red coat, and found she could not roll in the ash. She has sat by the basin three days with the coat over her head on the line, deciding.
unique_habit: Rubs the ash between her fingers and looks at it, the way a dyer looks at a dye, and says what colour it would take.

appearance.notes: a Vale shift, her hands stained madder-red to the wrist that no washing gets out, barefoot, a pack beside her with the dyes still in it
